title: Establish Python feature ceiling and determine if circuit Cohen's d degradation matters
context: v12 circuits achieve rho>=0.97 (7/8), 0% clipping, span>225mV (8/8), but Cohen's d fails 6/18 pairs (ratio <75%). Two parallel experiments running: (1) Python MLP baseline with exact 8->64->5 architecture on full 44 records, (2) analog emulation MLP applying empirical py->circuit transfer functions to all 44 records. Results determine whether circuit optimization is needed or whether the feature definitions themselves are the bottleneck.

success_criteria.target: Determine if d degradation causes >1% accuracy loss
success_criteria.measurement_method: Compare Python MLP vs analog emulation MLP accuracy

decision_tree: IF Python baseline < 96%: Feature definitions are the bottleneck, not circuits. Must redesign features or accept lower ceiling.
IF Python baseline >= 96% AND emulation >= 94%: Cohen's d compression is tolerable. Proceed to full ngspice validation.
IF Python baseline >= 96% AND emulation < 94%: Cohen's d compression matters. Must optimize circuits (reduce clamp compression, increase gain).
IF both results similar: v12 is sufficient. Proceed to full 44-record ngspice + MLP retraining.
constraints: Do NOT modify circuits until both experiments complete
Use EXACT 8->64->5 MLP architecture matching analog classifier
Full 44-record inter-patient protocol (DS1 train, DS2 test)
risk_factors: Python baseline may be <<96% with only 8 features (39-feature RF was 94.1%)
Analog emulation transfer functions built from only 6 records may not generalize
MLP may be more sensitive to d compression than RF was on the 6-record test
